key_results: NPP and focus align at low n but diverge at high n.
Mach-stem information extends the theoretical model to high n.
Four pressure contributions determine total NPP.

mechanisms.summary: Mach-stem/incident-wave forcing modifies the internal wave envelope; shock, relaxation, fluctuation, and expansion effects jointly set NPP.

evidence_candidates.claim: Focus-point and negative-peak-pressure locations align at low gas-liquid wave-speed ratio but diverge at high ratio.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Complete Ms/liquid case matrix shows NPP location becoming approximately constant at high n while the theoretical focus continues its decreasing trend.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Five-equation model has no phase transition, so cavitation itself is not resolved.

evidence_candidates.claim: Including Mach-stem motion improves the theoretical internal-wave envelope for high wave-speed-ratio cases.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Ray-tracing model switches the disturbance initiator from incident shock to Mach stem where appropriate.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Two-dimensional cylindrical geometry and fitted Mach-stem trajectory.

evidence_candidates.claim: The negative peak pressure results from the combined shock, relaxation, fluctuation, and expansion-wave effects rather than expansion-wave focusing alone.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Pressure histories and wave-count comparison show the focus maximizes the expansion-wave contribution, while NPP has the largest total pressure drop.
evidence_candidates.limitations: No cavitation phase transition; pressure-factor decomposition requires further validation.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Multi-contribution pressure mechanism in early shock-droplet interaction.
